title: Deep health gates and degraded-mode autoscale protection for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: During recent simulated region failovers and one production incident, transient probe failures and cold-starts caused the control plane autoscaler to rapidly scale down healthy replicas or fail to scale up in the target region. The result was cascading request failures and SLO breaches for request latency and availability.

Problem statement: Our current readiness/liveness checks are too binary and tightly coupled to autoscaler decisions. Shallow (TCP/HTTP 200) checks are used for routing, while deeper readiness (model loaded, KV cache warmed, third-party auth reachable) is conflated in the same probe or triggers outside a stabilization window. Autoscaler responds to immediate healthy replica counts leading to oscillation during failover. We need a principled design that: (1) separates shallow routing health from deep readiness; (2) provides autoscaler signals that are smoothed and prioritized by SLO impact; (3) integrates explicit degraded-mode and circuit-breaker behavior to shed non-essential traffic gracefully during capacity gaps.

Goal: Implement "deep health gates" and autoscaler protection rules so multi-region failover and transient degradations do not cause amplifying autoscaler churn and SLO violations. The solution should be observable, testable in canary, and have a staged rollout with rollback knobs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Shallow vs Deep checks: Node-level shallow probe stays fast and only used for LB. Deep readiness endpoint reports component-level readiness (model loaded, KV cache status, external auth, token fetch) and exposes a reason code when not ready.
2) Autoscaler integration: HPA/Custom autoscaler consumes a smoothed healthyReplicaCount derived from a 60s sliding window and cross-AZ majority heuristics. Immediate probe flips must not trigger scale-to-zero within 3 minutes of a region failover event.
3) Degraded-mode circuit breakers: Route-level circuit breaker that can (a) opt-in to degraded responses (400-level with degraded header), (b) reject background/batch requests first, and (c) progressively shed lowest-priority tenants using token-bucket ranking.
4) Observability: Dashboards show healthyReplicaCount, probe flip rate, scaledown events, and SLO error budget burn. Alerts for autoscaler churn > 3 events per 15m.
5) Canary & rollout: Deploy to canary region (eu-central-1-canary) and pass chaos tests (engineered GC pauses, node reboots) without SLO breaches for 1h.
6) Documentation: Confluence runbook and API docs for deep readiness endpoints and circuit breaker config.
design_notes:
- Deep readiness endpoint will be a /ready?detail=true endpoint that returns terse reason codes (e.g., MODEL_UNLOADED, KV_COLD, AUTH_TIMEOUT). We intentionally avoid large payloads.
- Shallow liveness remains single-line 200 for kube/HEALTH.
- Autoscaler will compute healthyReplicaCount = max(soft_count, majority_count) where soft_count is the 60s-windowed mean of readiness successes and majority_count requires >50% AZs reporting >min_replicas. This prevents single-AZ flaps from scaling down cross-region capacity.
- Implement transient-hold: after a region failover event is detected by the router (route-change webhook), mark targets with a 180s hold that delays scale-to-zero actions.
- Circuit breakers: per-route config with priority labels: essential, interactive, batch. Batch gets highest shedding priority. Shedding is controlled by an adaptive token bucket that reduces tokens under high latency and re-fills when tail latency improves.
- All configs expose feature flags for rollout and can be toggled by runtime flags in the control plane.
implementation_plan:
1) API: Add /ready?detail=true to runtime with minimal latency cost. (Owner: runtime-agent team)
2) Autoscaler: Extend controller to consume sliding-windowed readiness telemetry and cross-AZ majority. Add 180s transient-hold on detected region failovers. (Owner: autoscaler)
3) Circuit breaker: Add route-level config in control plane; implement token-bucket-based shedding in proxy. (Owner: gateway/proxy)
4) Observability: Add dashboards and alerts; instrument probe flip rate. (Owner: observability)
5) Tests: Unit tests, integration in staging, chaos run in canary region. (Owner: SRE + QA)
6) Rollout: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global with 1h stability gate at each step.
7) Runbook: Update on-call runbook and failure-mode decision tree.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Deep readiness checks slow down container startup and increase pod churn. Mitigation: Make deep checks asynchronous and cache recent success for 30s; deep readiness should not be used by LB.
Risk: Complexity in autoscaler math introduces bugs. Mitigation: Ship as opt-in feature flag with telemetry and compare against baseline for two weeks.
Risk: Incorrect shedding ordering could impact paying customers. Mitigation: Allow tenant opt-out and expose emergency override for support team.
Risk: Edge cases during simultaneous multi-tenant bursts. Mitigation: Add per-tenant quotas and backpressure feedback to clients.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for readiness reason codes and lightweight stubs.
- Integration test: simulate model load failures and verify healthyReplicaCount behavior.
- Chaos: induce GC pause and node reboot in canary region and verify autoscaler does not scale to zero for held period.
- Load test: simulate 2x traffic with 25% cold-model requests and verify degraded-mode shedding sequence respects priority labels.
- Post-deploy verification: measure probe flip-rate, scaledown events, and SLO latency/budget for 24h.
rollout_plan: Canary (eu-central-1-canary) with traffic shadowing for 24h -> 10% traffic for 1h -> 50% traffic for 2h -> global with 1h gates. Feature flags enabled per-cluster to allow immediate rollback. SRE to run manual checks at each gate and abort on any SLO regression.

notes: This ticket intentionally separates shallow routing probes (fast, LB-only) from deep readiness (component and warm state). The implementation will be gated behind a feature flag and rolled out to canary clusters first. Focus on minimizing surface area that autoscalers observe as unhealthy.
